main_text.p: calamitatum & miseriarum metus ac denunciatio mœrore lenit: & idem miseri-cordia præstat, demortuorum cognatorum, vel aliorum qui cari fuerunt, [illegible, ~9 letters] & obtestatione adhibita. ConsolatioAd ἰδικά porrò mo-rata & conciliatia argumenta quod attinet, à perfona illa partim noftra, partim eorū ad quos scribimus petitur. rum argu-menta ἰδικά morata & conciliantia.In noftra amoris ac beneuolentię significatio: commemoratio officiorū: societas ægritudinis: literarū, vel infrequentię, vel breuitatis excusatio: extenuatio viriū in consolando mo-desta: metus etiā nonnunquam profesio prodeft: ne temerè, vel cōfidere ipsi, vel inanem aliis iniicere spē videamur. In aliena laus vtilis est ac cōmendatio pietatis, doctrinę, prudentię, magnitudinis animi: amoris itidem, studij, officij illius quē consolari cupimus: & hac ipsa quasi languen-tes excitari solent.Collocatio argumentorum in singulis consolatoriarum epistolarum partibus.Sunt autem, vt de argumentorum istorum collocatione atq; tractatione agamus, quatuor consolatoriarum epistolarum partes: Exordium, propositio, confirmatio & conclusio. Exordia constant, vel Exordia consolatoria.δείξει τῆς συμπαθείας [?] significatione doloris, meroris, luctus ex amici casu aduerso perceptì, & modesta virium atq; ingenij nostri in consolando extenuatione. lib. 1. e-pist.5.

page.notes: Greek words are uncertain: the word after "fuerunt," is illegible; "ἰδικά" in the note and text, and "δείξει τῆς συμπαθείας" in the Exordia note, are copied with [?] where the scan is faint. The left-margin note beginning "rum argu-" is partly cut off at its top. The reference "pist.5." at the foot is set right-aligned and read as "e-pist.5." after the hyphenated "e-" at the line end. No catchword or signature is visible.
